dots-3-note-preview:free.description:
Dots Studio’s Dots3-Note Preview accepts text, images, video, and audio, and returns text only. With a context window of512,000 tokens (524,288 tokens), it can support long-document and long-duration video analysis. Video can be interpreted as a combined audiovisual signal when an audio track is available. The model supports function calling, tool selection, JSON Schema-validated structured output, and reasoning tokens.

It is suited to transcription, video description, chart and document reading, and question answering grounded in visual or audio input. Other supported uses include general knowledge, instruction following, mathematical and logical reasoning, code generation, and multi-step agent workflows that adapt through interactive tasks and memory updates. Its MoE architecture has280B total parameters and16B active parameters per token; sparse and sliding-window attention patterns help reduce computation while supporting its long context. It is positioned as the smallest and fastest model in the Dots3 family. The model is open-weight and available in BF16 and FP8 formats.
dots-3-note-preview:free.name: Dots Studio: Dots3-Note Preview (free)

ernie-5.5-flash-preview:free.description:
ERNIE-5.5-Flash-Preview(free)  is a preview model in Baidu’s ERNIE5.5 Flash series. It uses a sparse Mixture of Experts (MoE) architecture with280 billion total parameters and14 billion activated parameters per token. Its context window is1 million tokens, and it is designed for efficient reasoning and generation at more than200 tokens per second. The preview is primarily available through API access.

The model supports advanced reasoning, tool calling, and long-context processing. It is suited to code generation and checking, automated test scripts, and agent workflows that divide work into search, execution, verification, and repair. It can also help with deep research across long documents, source organization, and research reports, as well as copywriting, video scripts, game materials, and3D scene generation through tool calling.

AutomationBench and SpreadsheetBench results each ranked it first among eight benchmarks on2026年11月11日. These results should be viewed alongside reported limitations: third-party evaluations raised possible test-data memorization on HumanEval, OpenBookQA, and GSM8K, and user feedback noted that coding consistency was not particularly strong. No standalone overall score was published, and some benchmark results were disputed.
ernie-5.5-flash-preview:free.name: Baidu: ERNIE-5.5-Flash-Preview (free)

flint-v1.0:free.description:
Flint is Recursive's first model: an open-weight mixture-of-experts language model built for coding agents. It has 39.8 billion total parameters with approximately 2.5 billion active per token, arranged across 49 layers — 2 dense layers followed by 47 mixture-of-experts layers. It accepts text input and produces text output, supports multi-turn tool use, and ships under the Apache 2.0 license, so it can be used commercially, modified, and redistributed. Recursive says Flint was largely built by its own AI research system, Eureka Machine.

The model is aimed at agentic coding workflows: investigating codebases, fixing bugs, implementing features, and writing tests. Its 262,000-token context is shared between prompt and output, enough to hold a meaningful slice of a mid-sized repository alongside the agent's reasoning trace without aggressive chunking or retrieval tricks; Recursive recommends an output budget of at least 32,768 tokens. Typical uses include helping developers write code, building small applications, and solving programming problems.

Flint can run on a single B300 or H200 GPU per replica using an SGLang serving kit, and Recursive reports throughput of 125 or more tokens per second on an M4 Pro and 150 or more on a 64GB NVIDIA GPU. The BF16 checkpoint weighs around 80 GB. It was free to access on OpenRouter at launch.
flint-v1.0:free.name: Recursive: Flint (free)

gemma-4-26b-a4b-it:free.description:
Gemma 4 26B A4B is an open-weight multimodal model from Google DeepMind built on a Mixture-of-Experts architecture with 26B total parameters and 4B active parameters at inference. It accepts text, image, and video input and produces text output, with a 256K token context window. Images can have variable aspect ratios and resolutions, and video is processed up to 60 seconds at 1 frame per second. The model supports over 140 languages, native system prompts, native function calling, and a configurable thinking mode.

It is designed for coding assistance in IDEs and agentic workflows, code generation, debugging and refactoring, scientific and mathematical problem solving, research support, document parsing and OCR, image-based question answering, video understanding, and large-scale document processing and RAG systems. Its strengths include a balance of intelligence against parameter efficiency, near-frontier performance, and the ability to run on consumer GPUs and workstations. Reported throughput is about 91 tokens per second with a time to first token of about 0.92 seconds, and it is said to run within 2% of the 31B dense model on every benchmark tested.

Gemma 4 26B A4B is licensed under Apache 2.0 and available for commercial use. It can be accessed through Cloudflare, Google Cloud Vertex AI, NVIDIA NGC, and Azure ML, and API access is offered by 7 providers. It does not natively support audio; audio processing is available only in the smaller E2B, E4B, and 12B models. The model is positioned as the mid-range mainstay between the edge-oriented small models and the enterprise-oriented large model in the Gemma 4 family.
gemma-4-26b-a4b-it:free.name: Google: Gemma 4 26B A4B  (free)

lfm-3-1.7b:free.description:
LFM3-1.7B is an open-weight, text-only language model from Liquid AI with about 1.73 billion parameters and 24 layers. It uses a new tri-hybrid architecture combining 13 gated short convolution layers, 5 sliding window attention layers, and 6 global attention layers. The model accepts text input and produces text output, supports tool calling and structured outputs, and handles a context of 256K tokens covering input and output combined. It supports 16 languages: English, Arabic, Chinese, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Spanish, Vietnamese, Thai, Indonesian, Hindi, Russian, and Polish.

The model is designed for local agents and domain-specific applications and is post-trained for agent harnesses such as Hermes Agent, Pi, and OpenClaw. It runs on Transformers, vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, MLX, and ONNX Runtime, and is available in BF16, FP8, NVFP4, GGUF, MLX, and ONNX quantization formats. In 4-bit quantized form it uses about 1 GB of memory, and at 128K-token context it uses about 1.6 GB of cache.

LFM3-1.7B suits local agents, tool calling, structured outputs, structured JSON extraction, answering from retrieved documents, domain-specific fine-tuning, tool selection in a 108-tool phone app, and learning new languages. Retrieval or retrieval-augmented generation is recommended for knowledge-intensive tasks. It is not recommended for agentic coding or complex multi-step reasoning.
lfm-3-1.7b:free.name: LiquidAI: LFM3-1.7B (free)

ling-3.2-flash:free.description:
inclusionAI: Ling3.2 Flash, from Ant Ling, uses a native multimodal architecture that combines vision and language within the model itself. It accepts text, images, and video as input and produces text output, with a1 million token context window. The model has560 billion total parameters, with25 billion parameters active per token.

This model is suited to complex visual understanding, document and frame analysis,3D understanding and interaction, medical multimodal work, and multimodal long-horizon agent tasks. It can also support visual feedback loops in which the model inspects its own renders. Video input is limited to thirty seconds per clip, one clip per request, and thirty-two sampled frames; requests can contain up to forty images, with each image under16384 by784 pixels.

Ling3.2 Flash is positioned above Ling3.1 Flash in Ant Ling's model selection table. Ant reported that it beat Opus5 on ZEROBench and Vision2Web, but no scores were provided. The API has a global rate limit of two requests per second, and synchronous calls have a90-second timeout; streaming is recommended for production use.
ling-3.2-flash:free.name: inclusionAI: Ling 3.2 Flash (free)

nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free.description:
Nemotron 3 Ultra is NVIDIA's final and best model in the Nemotron 3 family: an open frontier-reasoning and orchestration model built on a Hybrid Transformer-Mamba mixture-of-experts architecture. It has 550 billion total parameters with 55 billion active parameters. It uses LatentMoE for improved accuracy and includes MTP layers for faster inference through native speculative decoding. The model was pretrained in NVFP4 format and post-trained with Supervised Fine Tuning, Reinforcement Learning, and Multi-teacher On-Policy Distillation. It takes text input and returns text output, with a 1 million token context window.

The model is designed for multi-step reasoning and planning, agent orchestration, coding agents, deep research, and complex enterprise tasks. It supports function calling through tools and tool_choice parameters, structured outputs via a JSON schema in response_format, and inference time reasoning budget control. NVIDIA positions it for long-running autonomous agent workflows and high-throughput inference in high-volume agent pipelines. It outperforms state-of-the-art open LLMs on RULER at 1M context length. The free endpoint is rate limited.

NVIDIA releases open weights, training data, and recipes, including pre-trained, post-trained, and quantized checkpoints along with training datasets. On OpenRouter the model is served by three providers: DeepInfra, Baseten, and Venice.
nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free.name: NVIDIA: Nemotron 3 Ultra (free)

nemotron-3.5-lightning:free.description:
Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is NVIDIA's open-weight, text-only Mixture-of-Experts model built for the execution layer of high-volume agentic workloads. It uses a hybrid architecture that interleaves Mamba-2 layers with MoE layers and select attention layers, and it is distilled from NVIDIA's frontier Nemotron 3 Ultra model. It handles prompts of up to 1 million tokens and accepts text input while producing text output.

The model is trained for agentic tool use across popular agent harnesses such as OpenClaw and Hermes, and it incorporates DFlash speculative decoding to reduce per-token latency. It is released under the OpenMDW-1.0 license with downloadable weights, training data, and recipes, and it can be post-trained with NVIDIA NeMo for domain-specific tools, workflows, and policies. It runs on a single supported device and ships alongside NVIDIA Switchyard, a model-routing system that directs each workflow step to the model that best fits its cost, latency, and capability needs.

It suits agentic and high-volume operational work: personal assistants that handle email, calendars, and bookings; financial data extraction, policy checks, and summaries; security alert triage and investigation; network and billing support in telecom; catalog, order, and inventory workflows in retail; pull-request review and code fixes; and customer support automation. Its only documented limitation is that it is text-only.
nemotron-3.5-lightning:free.name: NVIDIA: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (free)

nemotron-3.5-super-vl:free.description:
Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is NVIDIA's multimodal model for agentic work that mixes visual and textual inputs. It accepts text, images, documents, GUI screenshots, and video, and returns text. Built on a 120-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts architecture with 12 billion active parameters per inference, it pairs a hybrid Mamba-Transformer design with NVFP4 quantization and quantization-aware distillation, multi-token prediction, and LiLiCorr speculative decoding. It runs on a single NVIDIA Blackwell GPU, and is offered as an NVIDIA NIM microservice served with vLLM on platforms including Blackwell and Hopper, as well as on Baseten and Nscale dedicated inference. It can be post-trained with the open-source NVIDIA NeMo library using supervised fine-tuning, low-rank adaptation, and reinforcement learning.

The model suits tasks where an agent must read both words and pictures: web research agents for competitive intelligence, market analysis, knowledge discovery, and automated information gathering; document intelligence over complex documents containing text, images, tables, charts, and page layouts; customer service that interprets customer documents and images and calls service tools for multi-step requests; video understanding for video search, content moderation, advertising, retail workflows, and event analysis; and agentic coding workflows that require reasoning and multi-step task completion. It is also positioned for virtual machine and graphical user interface automation.

NVIDIA reports up to 5x higher throughput per GPU than comparable open-source models on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index agentic tasks, over 600 TPS on the Baseten endpoint, and completion of 10,000 tasks 4x faster than Qwen3.8 Flash Next on 4 NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs in NVIDIA's agentic coding benchmark while keeping competitive SWE-Bench Pro accuracy. Accuracy is described as comparable to NVIDIA's largest reasoning model with roughly one-fifth the parameters, and the model is described as the fastest open agentic model in its class. The free endpoint is not suitable for uploading confidential information or personal data.
nemotron-3.5-super-vl:free.name: NVIDIA: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL (free)

xing4.0-29b-a4b:free.description:
Xing4.0 29B A4B is a lightweight agentic large language model released by China Telecom Artificial Intelligence Technology Co., Ltd. on September 17, 2026. It uses a Mixture-of-Experts architecture with 29B total parameters and 4B active parameters per inference, supports text input and text output, and offers a natively 256K context that can be extended to 512K. Reasoning is enabled by default and can be turned off. The model is open-sourced under the Apache-2.0 license and succeeds the TeleChat series, now renamed Xing.

The model is built for agentic work: it handles complex task understanding, task planning, tool calling, and autonomous execution. It is well suited to code development, data analysis, office automation, life services, and agent applications that need multi-step planning and independent operation. Benchmarks show 75.0 on SWE-bench Verified and 57.5 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, and it ranked third on SuperCLUE Agent with 93.52. It outperforms same-size competitors on SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench 2.1.

Xing4.0 29B A4B is the first fully domestically produced lightweight agentic large model, trained entirely on Ascend compute and the MindSpore framework. It can run complex autonomous workflows on a single consumer desktop GPU, and after 4-bit quantization it needs about 15GB of VRAM for local deployment. A GGUF version runs in local tools such as LM Studio with at least 32GB of memory. It supports private deployment, is compatible with LLaMA-Factory and Mindformers fine-tuning frameworks, and is adapted to SGLang, vLLM, and KTransformers inference frameworks. Weights and configuration files are provided in Hugging Face Transformers format.
xing4.0-29b-a4b:free.name: XingChen: Xing4.0 29B A4B (free)

humansand/ampersand-v0.1.description: Ampersand v0.1 is a collaborator model from Humans& for shared goals, group conversations, and long-running collaboration. Its Responses API supports text, reasoning, client-side function tools, and implicit prompt caching.
humansand/ampersand-v0.1.name: Ampersand v0.1

nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-free.description: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is an open-weight reasoning and chat model for long-running agents, sub-agent work, chatbots, and RAG systems. The model has 30B parameters with 3B active per token, in a hybrid Mixture-of-Experts design that interleaves Mamba-2 and MoE layers with a few attention layers. It has a 1M token context window and supports tool calling and structured outputs. The provider may retain prompts and responses for model improvement.
nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-free.name: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning Free

recursive/flint-v1.0.description: Flint is Recursive's open-weight mixture-of-experts model for agentic coding, with 40 billion total parameters and 2.5 billion active per token. It returns its reasoning alongside the answer and supports tool calling and structured outputs.
recursive/flint-v1.0.name: Flint

reflection/beam-free.description: Beam is Reflection’s reasoning model for coding and agentic workflows, combining strong coding capabilities with fast, low-latency inference.
reflection/beam-free.name: Beam 1.0 (Free)

stealth/glyph-cluster.description: Glyph Cluster is an anonymous reasoning model in early access. Prompts and outputs will be retained by the provider.
